newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH LOCAL GOVERNMENTS EXPECT BUDGET DEFICITS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH LOCAL GOVERNMENTS EXPECT BUDGET DEFICITS.

text.p: After a few years in surplus, the sum of municipalities' budgets will turn into a 2.6 billion markka deficit in 1996 and into a 7.0 billion deficit in 1997, the Association of Finnish Local Authorities said on Wednesday.
The fall would follow lower state contributions, it said in a report.
Municipal budgets after net investment and debt servicing last year generated a 1.5 billion markka surplus.
Municipal debt would fall to 23.4 billion markka at the end of this year from 26.0 billion at end-1995 but rise to 24.5 percent at end-1997, the association said.

At gross level, i.e. before net investments and debt servicing, municipalities margins would fall from last year's 13 billion markka surplus to 9.9 billion next year and to 5.5 billion markka in 1997, in a base scenario assuming 3.5 percent annual GDP growth.
"In a slow growth scenario (GDP growth at 2.0 pct until 1999), the gross margin would turn negative in 1998 and be -2.8 billion markka (in 1999)," the association said.
For many municipalities, that would be critical, it said.
The association's managing director Jussi-Pekka Alanen told a seminar for local government managers that media had conveyed too positive a picture of the local governments' situation.
"Things should not be looked at only from the situation at this stage but rather at where we are headed," he said.
He was surprised of the lack of debate.
"There has really been very little debate about this although local elections are coming up," he noted.
Finland will hold local and European parliament elections on the same day, October 20.
